**Assessment**
- **Mostly yes.** In 2024 Scholz publicly defended press freedom, critical journalism, public questioning, and protest rights. I found no reliable evidence that he ran propaganda, censored outlets, or directly pressured owners/journalists.
- **Main caveat:** Germany still had a structural intelligence-oversight problem, and there was some indirect criticism that pro-Palestinian speech was chilled. That is a real negative, but it is not the same as Scholz personally running a censorship regime.

This is the main structural negative on information access and independent oversight. | 4B.6, 3B.8, 4B.4 |
| Counterweight | [Art world accusing German government of choking pro-Palestinian speech](https://www.euronews.com/culture/2024/01/24/art-world-accusing-german-government-of-choking-pro-palestinian-speech) | Euronews | 2024-01-24 | https://www.euronews.com/culture/2024/01/24/art-world-accusing-german-government-of-choking-pro-palestinian-speech | This reports criticism that a Berlin funding clause chilled pro-Palestinian expression. It is a real counterweight, but indirect and not proof Scholz personally ordered censorship. | 4B.6, 4B.3 |

**Search Gap**
- I found **no reliable direct evidence** in 2024 that Scholz used state media, disinformation campaigns, direct journalist pressure, or ownership leverage to manipulate public information.
- The negative evidence is mostly **structural or indirect**: the BND surveillance ruling and separate criticism of speech climate around Gaza-related issues.
- Netting that out, the record is **more protective than repressive** on media and information access.
